note: Risks to delivery, with an owner and a mitigation. A risk with no owner is a wish. Reviewed at each wave boundary.

risks.title: Divergent git histories between the cloud session and the local clone
risks.detail: Five commits of screen work (registries, parts network, accounting, CRM, customer app) existed only in the cloud container and were never on GitHub. A reset to the pushed branch silently rewound the working tree to a state missing 62 built screens; the registry caught it by reporting 52 rendering instead of 114.
risks.mitigation: The five commits were cherry-picked onto the pushed branch. Going forward: the registry's `rendered` count is checked after any branch operation, and the session pushes through the user rather than assuming its own history is canonical.

risks.title: This environment cannot push to the remote
risks.detail: The sandbox proxy returns 403 on push; fetch works. Every handover therefore needs a patch file and a manual push, which is slow and loses commit authorship.
risks.mitigation: Connect the GitHub account to the environment. Until then: commit locally, hand over `git format-patch` output, verify the pushed hash before continuing.

risks.title: Three GitHub PATs were pasted in chat
risks.detail: Tokens appear in the transcript and possibly in provider logs. At least one was auto-revoked by GitHub secret scanning; the others are unconfirmed.
risks.mitigation: Rotate all three, add gitleaks to CI, and never paste a credential into chat again — use the environment's connection instead.

risks.title: The repository is public
risks.detail: It carries the design bundle, 235 production screenshots, the RBAC matrix, the API contract and now the full execution plan — a detailed map of a commercial product's internals.
risks.mitigation: Make it private. Costs nothing and changes nothing about the work.

risks.title: Shared-file contention across ten concurrent product agents
risks.detail: routes/index.tsx, repository.ts, rbac.ts and the migrations are touched by every agent. Simultaneous edits are the specific failure that turns an 8-week parallel build back into a 25-week serial one.
risks.mitigation: OWNERSHIP.json serialises them through Agent 01, and the registry-driven route table removes routes/index.tsx from the contention set entirely.

risks.title: The design bundle violates its own brand rules
risks.detail: Dashboard.dc.html uses #06B6D4 (teal) in two gradients, which handoff/README.md §7 forbids. The port reproduced it faithfully, so the violation is now in Dashboard.tsx:73 and :398.
risks.mitigation: Replace with #0AA3EE from the token set — same darkening intent, inside the palette. Decided rather than silently tuned: the token gate keeps flagging it until it is fixed, and narrowing the gate's hue band to hide it is explicitly not the fix.

risks.title: Estimates assume no rework
risks.detail: 265 engineer-days assumes each capability is built once. Backend contract changes after W1 would force rework across W2's ten agents simultaneously.
risks.mitigation: Freeze the contract package at the end of W1 and version it; contract changes after that go through Agent 03 as a scheduled migration, not an ad-hoc edit.

risks.title: Feature-map screens have no design, only a screenshot and a templated spec
risks.detail: 175 of 402 capabilities are specified only by a screenshot and four templated fields. Fidelity expectations cannot be the same as for designed screens.
risks.mitigation: They are built through the feature kit and reproduce the reference's structure and empty states honestly. Where the reference is empty, the empty state ships — inventing rows would make unbuilt features look shipped.

risks.title: Twelve capabilities depend on hardware or paid services we do not have
risks.detail: Drone inspection, VR showroom, AR guides, wearables, security cameras, digital signage, blockchain, quantum, voice — all categorised EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCY in the registry.
risks.mitigation: Each ships complete UI, a real adapter interface, a mocked contract and an explicit unconfigured state, with the dependency named. None is ever labelled 'coming soon'.

risks.title: Mock-to-API swap could silently change behaviour
risks.detail: 114 screens currently render from fixtures. Swapping the repository for HTTP touches every one of them at once.
risks.mitigation: The database seeds from src/data/generated/tables.ts, so the seeded API renders exactly what the fixtures render, and every existing smoke assertion must still pass after the swap. A failing assertion is the swap being wrong, not the test being stale.

risks.title: Agents claiming completion without evidence
risks.detail: A subagent reporting 'done' is a claim, not a verification — and at ten concurrent agents the claims arrive faster than they can be read.
risks.mitigation: Agent 03 re-runs the Definition of Done rather than trusting the report, and the registry's evidence[] must name a screenshot or test artefact before status rises above IMPLEMENTED.
